patches.value: Fix arbitrary t>0, put J=[t/2,3t/2], and choose compact C from H003 so u(x,s)=q for every x∉C and s∈J. First establish the ambient measure fact needed for M001. Fix arbitrary compact K⊂ℝⁿ. By M016 it is bounded, so choose R₀>0 with K contained in the closed Euclidean ball of radius R₀. Every coordinate of a point in that ball has absolute value at most R₀, so K⊆Q=∏_{i=1}^n[-R₀,R₀]. The set K is closed, hence Borel measurable in the Euclidean Borel measurable space. M013 computes the Lebesgue measure of Q as the product of the coordinate interval measures; M014 gives each factor as 2R₀. Thus μ(Q)=(2R₀)^n<∞, and monotonicity gives μ(K)≤μ(Q)<∞. Since K was arbitrary, Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is finite on compact sets. This also establishes the needed measurable-topological ambient: the measurable space is the Borel σ-algebra generated by Euclidean open sets, so every open set is measurable. Joint smoothness and the fact u=q on the open spatial complement of C throughout J imply, for all s∈J, every first spatial and time derivative vanishes outside C; differentiating these constant-zero fields in the open complement shows the second and mixed derivatives used in e_t also vanish there. Therefore e(·,t) is continuous with compact support in C. The real scalars form a normed additive commutative group, and the preceding ambient argument supplies all measure hypotheses of M001; apply M001 to obtain integrability of e(·,t). The same support reasoning gives continuity and vanishing off C for u_t, u_{x_j}, e and e_t throughout J. This proves all the claims in N001 for arbitrary t.
